## Grading {.unnumbered}

Course grades are letter grades, based on:

| Category                | Weight |
|:------------------------|:-------|
| Homework                | 10%    |
| Programming labs        | 30%    |
| Worksheets              | 15%    |
| Midterm 1               | 10%    |
| Midterm 2               | 10%    |
| Final exam              | 25%    |

I will assign final letter grades based on the weighted average of the categories above,
by the standard scale:

| Cumulative score         | Letter grade |
|:-------------------------|:-------------|
| 90% or higher            | A range      |
| 80% to just under 90%    | B range      |
| 70% to just under 80%    | C range      |
| 60% to just under 70%    | D range      |
| under 60%                | F            |

Thresholds for plus and minus grades are at my discretion.
The overall grade Canvas displays may be inaccurate;
the weights above are the ones that count.

### Homework and Worksheets {.unnumbered}

Homework assignments combine written work and programming.
Homework and worksheets are graded on completion,
meaning whether you made a solid effort to solve each problem:

- Complete: 100%
- Substantial effort: 80%
- Minimal effort: 40%
- Missing: 0%

The lowest worksheet score is dropped.

**Quiz 0** is a short quiz in the first week
that checks the CSCI 145 and precalculus material this course assumes.
It is graded on completion and counts as one worksheet,
and its main purpose is to show you (and me) what to review.

When writing up your work:

- Type all written work, in any tool you like.
  I recommend Markdown with LaTeX math (`$x^2$` for $x^2$),
  for example in a Quarto document or a Jupyter notebook,
  which you can then render to PDF.
  A full LaTeX document also works.
- Hand-drawn diagrams are welcome when they help illustrate a concept,
  as long as they are legible.
- Format code and pseudocode in a fixed-width font.
  Do not submit screenshots of your editor or terminal.
- Show your work.
  An answer alone will not get full credit,
  on homework or on exams.

### Labs {.unnumbered}

Weekly labs give hands-on programming practice,
with a TA available to answer questions during the lab period.
To get full credit, **you must both attend lab and submit the deliverable by its deadline**,
which will typically be 10pm on the Monday after the lab
(or the next class day, when that Monday is a holiday).

- If you do not attend lab but submit the deliverable on time,
  your score is multiplied by 0.5.
  This penalty is waived automatically for one lab;
  if you have a legitimate reason to miss more,
  contact me and the TA ahead of time.
- Attending a lab section other than your own requires permission from both me and the TA(s).
- Late lab submissions are not accepted.

### Exams {.unnumbered #exams}

The course has two in-class midterm exams,
tentatively on Wednesday, January 27 (week 4) and Wednesday, February 17 (week 7),
and a cumulative final exam during finals week,
in our classroom at the time WWU's
[finals schedule](https://registrar.wwu.edu/calendars/finals) assigns,
which is set by the lecture time:
Tuesday, March 16 for the 11:00 sections (CRNs 13745 and 13746)
and Thursday, March 18 for the 9:00 sections (CRNs 13747 and 13748),
both 10:30am--12:30pm.

- Each midterm lasts 50 minutes.
- The final exam lasts 120 minutes.

You do not bring your own notes to an exam.
Instead, I hand out a printed note sheet with each exam,
which gives the definitions, laws and notation that the exam uses.
The same sheets are on this site ahead of time,
on the [exam note sheets](note-sheets.qmd) page,
so you can study with the sheet you will have in the exam.

If you know in advance that you will be unable to take an exam at the scheduled time,
let me know at least one week before the exam,
and we may be able to reschedule it.

### Grading Questions {.unnumbered}

If you have a question about a grade,
send it to me in writing, as a Canvas message (see [Communication](#communication)),
within 48 hours of the graded work being returned.
You will never lose points for asking.
